properties.areaDesc: Western Arctic Coast
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 7 at 3:01PM AKDT until October 10 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...High surf expected. Water levels of 2 to 4 feet above
the normal high tide line, peaking during high tide.

* WHERE...Western Arctic Coast from Point Hope south.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Thursday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A low in the Western Bering Sea will send
a front moving east in the coast, resulting in south to
southeast winds ramping up Thursday morning through Friday,
before diminishing through Saturday. Sea levels will remain
elevated through Friday before gradually subsiding Friday
night into Saturday.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 7 at 3:01PM AKDT until October 10 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Water levels of 4 to 6
feet above the normal high tide line, peaking during high tide.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Thursday to 4 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Localized beach erosion may occur. In Hooper Bay,
water may approach beach property and access to the airstrip
may be threatened.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Areas north of Hooper Bay are expected to
see lower water levels around 2 to 4 feet above the normal
high tide line. A low in the Western Bering Sea will send a
front moving east in the coast, resulting in south to
southeast winds ramping up Thursday morning through Friday,
before diminishing through Saturday. Sea levels will remain
elevated through Friday before gradually subsiding Friday
night into Saturday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 7 at 6:59PM EDT by NWS Gaylord MI
properties.description:
At 659 PM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking gusty showers and embedded
isolated thunderstorms along a line extending from Bisma Township to
near Morey. Movement was southeast at 35 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Houghton Lake, Grayling, Ossineke, Roscommon, Lewiston, St. Helen,
The Town Of Hubbard Lake, Mio, Atlanta, Prudenville, Lachine, Comins,
Sharon, Frederic, McKinley, Long Rapids, Hillman, Lovells, Curran,
and North Higgins Lake.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.areaDesc: Mobile Coastal; Baldwin Coastal; Escambia Coastal; Santa Rosa Coastal; Okaloosa Coastal
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 7 at 5:55PM CDT until October 11 at 6:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...In Alabama, Mobile Coastal and Baldwin Coastal
Counties. In Florida, Escambia Coastal, Santa Rosa Coastal and
Okaloosa Coastal Counties.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Cameron, TX
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 7 at 5:28PM CDT until October 7 at 7:30PM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Cameron County in deep south Texas...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 528 PM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Port Of Brownsville, Southmost, Cameron Park, Downtown
Brownsville, Brownsville, Lincoln Park, Rivera High School, El
Jardin Elementary School, South Point, Brownsville South Padre
Island International Airport, Perkins Middle School, Villa
Pancho, Gonzalez Elementary School, North Brownsville Little
League, Lopez High School, Southmost Elementary School, Gallegos
Elementary School, Besteiro Middle School, Brownsville Public
Library Southmost Branch and Brownsville Fire Department Station
Six.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

FROM FRIDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH FRIDAY EVENING...
...FIRE WEATHER WATCH FOR HIGH WINDS AND ACTIVE WILDFIRES IN EFFECT
FROM SATURDAY MORNING THROUGH SATURDAY EVENING....

The National Weather Service in Elko has issued a Fire Weather
Watch, which is in effect from Friday afternoon through Friday
evening. a Fire Weather Watch has also been issued from Saturday
morning through Saturday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire weather zones 424, 437, 438, 469, and
470.

* WIND...Sustained winds up to 15-20 mph, gusts 25-30 mph Friday
afternoon. Sustained winds up to 20-25 mph, gusts 35-40 mph
Saturday.

* HUMIDITY...Humidity as low as 12-15% Friday. 19-22% Saturday.

* HIGHEST THREAT...Highest threat will be in fire zones 437 and
469 due to active wildfires in the area along with high winds.

* IMPACTS...any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
High winds may impact active wildfires to spread further. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A fire weather watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
red flag warnings.

properties.headline: Tropical Cyclone Local Statement issued October 7 at 4:10PM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
HLSMOB

This product covers portions of southwest Alabama...northwest Florida...south
central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.

**ISAIAS QUICKLY INTENSIFYING, FORECAST TO BE A HURRICANE BY THURSDAY
MORNING**

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch has been issued for Butler, Clarke,
Crenshaw, George, Greene, Monroe, Washington, and Wilcox
- A Hurricane Watch has been issued for Conecuh, Covington, and
Escambia

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Butler, Clarke,
Crenshaw, George, Greene, Monroe, Washington, and Wilcox
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Baldwin Central, Baldwin Coastal, Escambia Coastal, Mobile
Central, Mobile Coastal, Okaloosa Coastal, and Santa Rosa
Coastal
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Baldwin Inland, Conecuh,
Covington, Escambia, Escambia Inland, Mobile Inland, Okaloosa
Inland, and Santa Rosa Inland

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 630 miles south-southwest of Mobile AL or about 640 miles
southwest of Pensacola FL
- 22.7N 92.9W
- Storm Intensity 65 mph
- Movement East-northeast or 65 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Tropical Storm Isaias has strengthened and should continue to
intensify through Friday morning. Isaias is currently moving east-
northeast and should eventually turn northward and accelerate
towards the north central Gulf coast. As it nears the coast, wind
fields will expand with the potential for significant wind impacts
and a life threatening storm surge along and to the east of where
the hurricane makes landfall. There still remains uncertainty with
the eventual speed and track of the hurricane so everyone should
continue to closely monitor the latest forecast over the next few
days.

Areas of heavy rainfall and flooding are possible although with the
fast speed of the hurricane at landfall we are currently expecting 3
to 7 inches with localized amounts up to 10 inches near the coast.
In addition, a favorable environment for tornadoes will also develop
to the east of the track as it moves inland Friday through Saturday.

Please continue to monitor the latest forecast updates and follow
the advise of your local emergency management officials.

POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* SURGE:
Prepare for life-threatening surge having possible extensive impacts
across the Alabama and western Florida panhandle coasts. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Large areas of deep inundation with storm surge flooding
accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to buildings,
with several washing away. Damage compounded by floating
debris. Locations may be uninhabitable for an extended period.
- Large sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads
washed out or severely flooded. Flood control systems and
barriers may become stressed.
- Severe beach erosion with significant dune loss.
- Major damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers. Many
small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages with some lifted onshore and stranded.

Elsewhere across portions of southwest Alabama...northwest
Florida...south central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.,
little to no impact is anticipated.

* WIND:
Prepare for life-threatening wind having possible extensive impacts
across southwest and portions of south central Alabama and the western
Florida panhandle. Potential impacts in this area include:
- Considerable roof damage to sturdy buildings, with some having
window, door, and garage door failures leading to structural
damage. Mobile homes severely damaged, with some destroyed.
Damage accentuated by airborne projectiles. Locations may be
uninhabitable for weeks.
- Many large trees snapped or uprooted along with fences and
roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places.
- Large areas with power and communications outages.

Also, prepare for dangerous wind having possible limited to
significant impacts across portions of southeast Mississippi and the
remainder of southwest Alabama.

* TORNADOES:
Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across
coastal southwest Alabama, the western Florida panhandle, and
portions of southwest and south central Alabama. Potential impacts
include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across portions of southwest Alabama...northwest
Florida...south central Alabama...and inland southeast Mississippi.,
little to no impact is anticipated.

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across coastal Alabama and the western Florida
panhandle. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may
become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible significant
impacts across interior areas of southwest and south central Alabama.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.

* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For the latest detailed evacuation and shelter information...please
refer to your local emergency management agency at the phone number
or website listed below.
- Coastal Alabama:
- Baldwin County: 251-972-6807 or
www.baldwincountyal.gov/departments/EMA
- Mobile County: 251-460-8000 or mobilecountyema.gov
- Northwest Florida:
- Escambia County: 850-471-6400 or myescambia.com/beready
- Santa Rosa County: 850-983-5360 www.santarosa.fl.gov/emergency
- Okaloosa County: 850-651-7150 or myokaloosa.com/emergency-management
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

The next local statement will be issued by the National Weather
Service in Mobile AL around 10 PM CDT, or sooner if conditions
warrant.

**ISAIAS QUICKLY INTENSIFYING, FORECAST TO BE A HURRICANE BY THURSDAY
MORNING**


NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Tropical Storm Watch has been issued for Calhoun, Coffee,
Dale, Geneva, Henry, Houston, Inland Franklin, Jackson,
Northern Liberty, and Southern Liberty

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- A Storm Surge Watch and Hurricane Watch are in effect for
Coastal Bay, Coastal Gulf, and South Walton
- A Storm Surge Watch and Tropical Storm Watch are in effect for
Coastal Franklin, Coastal Jefferson, and Coastal Wakulla
- A Hurricane Watch is in effect for Central Walton and North
Walton
- A Storm Surge Watch is in effect for Coastal Dixie and Coastal
Taylor
- A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for Calhoun, Coffee, Dale,
Geneva, Henry, Holmes, Houston, Inland Bay, Inland Franklin,
Inland Gulf, Jackson, Northern Liberty, Southern Liberty, and
Washington

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 680 miles southwest of Panama City or about 690 miles
southwest of Apalachicola
- 22.7N 92.9W
- Storm Intensity 65 mph
- Movement East-northeast or 65 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

...TROPICAL STORM WATCH ISSUED FOR SOUTHEAST ALABAMA AND INLAND FLORIDA PANHANDLE
COUNTIES...

At 5 PM ET, Tropical Storm Isaias was still located in the Bay of
Campeche with maximum sustained winds of 65 mph and moving ENE at
8 mph. Isaias is forecast to turn northward in the next day or so and
accelerate in forward speed towards the central Gulf coast. Steady
strengthening is expected through much of the next couple of days,
although some weakening may be possible just before landfall. The wind
field is expected to expand considerably and may be lopsided towards
the east, leading to windier conditions for portions of our area.
There is still considerable uncertainty with both timing and track.
Conditions could begin to deteriorate across the Panhandle as early as
Friday morning.

Given the expected large size of Isaias, the wind threat may extend
well into the eastern portions of our area. An expected fast forward
speed may also lead to the wind threat extending further inland. Storm
surge will be possible along our whole coastline including the
Panhandle and Apalachee Bay. Inundation values of 5 to 7 feet above
ground level (AGL) are possible across the coastal Panhandle to Indian
Pass, 4 to 6 feet AGL from Indian Pass to the Steinhatchee River, and
2 to 4 feet AGL from the Steinhatchee River to Yankeetown.

Soggy conditions across the region from recent rainfall will make the
area more sensitive to flooding from additional heavy rainfall from
Isaias. Forecast rainfall totals of 3 to 7 inches is expected across
much of the area, with isolated amounts near 10 inches possible. If
realized, these values would likely cause at least isolated flash
flooding and some river flooding. It is too soon to determine exact
tornado impacts, but there is an elevated chance for tornadoes Friday
into Saturday.



POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:
Prepare for life-threatening rainfall flooding having possible
extensive impacts across the Florida Panhandle and portions of SE
Alabama. Potential impacts include:
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, and ditches may become
dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers may become
stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or washed
away. Many places where flood waters may cover escape routes.
Streets and parking lots become rivers of moving water with
underpasses submerged. Driving conditions become dangerous.
Many road and bridge closures with some weakened or washed out.

Prepare for dangerous rainfall flooding having possible limited to
significant impacts across southeast Alabama, southwest Georgia, and
the Florida Big Bend.

* WIND:
Prepare for dangerous wind having possible significant impacts across
Southeast Alabama and the Florida Panhandle. Potential impacts in this
area include:
- Some damage to roofing and siding materials, along with damage
to porches, awnings, carports, and sheds. A few buildings
experiencing window, door, and garage door failures. Mobile
homes damaged, especially if unanchored. Unsecured lightweight
objects become dangerous projectiles.
- Several large trees snapped or uprooted, but with greater
numbers in places where trees are shallow rooted. Several
fences and roadway signs blown over.
- Some roads impassable from large debris, and more within urban
or heavily wooded places. A few bridges, causeways, and access
routes impassable.
- Scattered power and communications outages, but more prevalent
in areas with above ground lines.

Also, prepare for hazardous wind having possible limited impacts
across the Florida Big Bend and Southeast Alabama.

Elsewhere across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend, and
southwestern Georgia, little to no impact is anticipated.

* SURGE:
Prepare for life-threatening surge having possible extensive impacts
across coastal Florida Panhandle and Florida Big Bend. Potential
impacts in this area include:
- Large areas of deep inundation with storm surge flooding
accentuated by battering waves. Structural damage to buildings,
with several washing away. Damage compounded by floating
debris. Locations may be uninhabitable for an extended period.
- Large sections of near-shore escape routes and secondary roads
washed out or severely flooded. Flood control systems and
barriers may become stressed.
- Severe beach erosion with significant dune loss.
- Major damage to marinas, docks, boardwalks, and piers. Many
small craft broken away from moorings, especially in
unprotected anchorages with some lifted onshore and stranded.

Elsewhere across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend,
southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia, little to no impact is
anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Prepare for a tornado event having possible limited impacts across the
Florida Panhandle. Potential impacts include:
- The occurrence of isolated tornadoes can hinder the execution
of emergency plans during tropical events.
- A few places may experience tornado damage, along with power
and communications disruptions.
- Locations could realize roofs peeled off buildings, chimneys
toppled, mobile homes pushed off foundations or overturned,
large tree tops and branches snapped off, shallow-rooted trees
knocked over, moving vehicles blown off roads, and small boats
pulled from moorings.

Elsewhere across eastern Florida panhandle, Florida Big Bend,
southeastern Alabama and southwestern Georgia, little to no impact is
anticipated.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials

* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:
Now is the time to check your emergency plan and emergency supplies
kit and take necessary actions to protect your family and secure your
home or business.

When making safety and preparedness decisions, do not focus on the
exact forecast track since hazards such as flooding rain, damaging
wind gusts, storm surge, and tornadoes extend well away from the
center of the storm.


If you live in a place particularly vulnerable to flooding, such as
near the Gulf of America or a large inland lake, in a low-lying or
poor drainage area, or near an already swollen river, plan to move to
safe shelter on higher ground.

Always heed the advice of local officials and comply with orders that
are issued. Do not
